text: I've created `filter.py`. It edits the given file in place, removes the JavaScript, and copies everything else through byte for byte. I ran it against about 45 XSS payloads and a clean sample document, and checked that the command line works. I haven't loaded any output in a real browser, so whether nothing executes rests on the parser following the HTML5 rules correctly. **How it works:** rather than rebuilding the page with a parser library, which would reformat it, the script walks through the raw text using the same rules browsers use to split HTML into tags. When nothing in a tag is dangerous, the original text is kept exactly as written. When an attribute has to go, only that attribute and the spacing next to it are cut. The file is read and written so that every byte (UTF-8, CRLF line endings) comes back unchanged. **What gets removed:** - **Script blocks:** ``, or to the end of the file if there isn't one. - **Leftover space:** one case leaves a stray space behind: `` becomes ``. To run it: ``` python3 filter.py page.html ```
